atAGlance: Chả cá chiên is fried fish cakes, usually with springy fish paste, dill or herbs, and lime-pepper salt dip or ginger fish sauce.
whatItIs: Chả cá chiên is fried fish cake, springy inside with crisp edges, often served as a snack, noodle topping, or rice side with chili, lime, or fish-sauce dip.
howToEnjoy: Eat while hot so the fish cake stays bouncy and the edges stay crisp. Dip lightly in fish-sauce dip or lime-pepper salt if served.
howLocalsOrder: Order chả cá chiên as a snack, side, or noodle topping. Ask for no chili or extra herbs before the plate lands.
worthKnowing: On Vietnamese menus, chả cá can mean fish cake, so chiên tells you this version is fried rather than turmeric-dill chả cá Lã Vọng.
goodToKnow: Contains fish and may be served with chili by default.
